assumptions: T is a finite tree with h>=1 non-leaf vertices.
Each vertex initially has one distinct token and destinations form a bijection on V(T).
Each round is a matching of tree edges, swapping endpoint tokens.

definitions.C_e: Number of token source-to-destination paths using e.
definitions.r_e: C_e/2; integral because bijections balance every tree cut.
definitions.LB_hub: max(D,max_x W_x), where D is the maximum token distance.

proved_claims: path endpoint transposition on length ell uses 2*ell-1 edge swaps, exchanges endpoints, restores internal tokens
deterministic cycle/path-transposition schedule uses polynomial O(nh) operations and singleton matching rounds

degenerate_cases.h_zero: A connected tree has one vertex or one edge. The singleton is identity (R=LB=0); on one edge identity takes 0 and the transposition takes 1 round with LB=1.
degenerate_cases.identity_for_h_positive: R=m=D=LB_hub=0; handled separately before dividing by LB_hub.

bounded_internal_vertex_theorem.novelty_classification: Elementary parameterized path-transposition consequence; factor depends quadratically on h and is not a constant-factor arbitrary-tree result.

arbitrary_caterpillar_question.question: Does a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm exist with R<=c*LB_hub for a universal constant c on caterpillars with arbitrary backbone length, leaves, and bijective destination permutations?

precise_failed_lemma.claim: After freezing the prefix in a left-to-right cut sweep, any remaining incoming token can be prepared for the next cut by at most one swap at the adjacent frontier center with one of its pendant leaves.
precise_failed_lemma.family: Bare spine v1...vt, one leaf x at v1, one leaf y at vt, no interior leaves; exchange tokens at x,y and fix all spine tokens.
precise_failed_lemma.failure: At cut v1v2 the token for x is at y, distance t-1 from v2, and v2 has no pendant leaf, so the claimed local swap is unavailable.
precise_failed_lemma.scope: Refutes one-hop local access only; D=t+1 already reflects endpoint distance, so it is not an OPT/LB_hub lower-bound family.

arbitrary_caterpillar_question.exact_remaining_obligation: Prove a token-preserving nonlocal frontier-exchange lemma with total delay O(max(D,max_i W(v_i))) and matching-round legality, or construct a schedule-independent asymptotic family disproving a universal factor.
adversarial_checks: opposing cut flows are balanced and contribute r(e) to both endpoint hub loads
adjacent busy hubs are constrained by W(v_i)=r(left edge)+r(right edge)+incorrect pendant leaves, but counts do not encode token identity order
fixed internal tokens can be temporarily displaced by path transposition and are restored exactly
a three-token cycle on a three-vertex spine resolves in two matching rounds and is not a counterexample
remote endpoint exchange falsifies local access but is paid for by token distance D

prior_art.citation: Alon, Chung, Graham (1994), Routing Permutations on Graphs via Matchings
prior_art.comparison: Same matching-round model; worst-case tree routing number <3n, not instance-relative LB_hub.

prior_art.citation: Zhang (1999), Optimal Bounds for Matching Routing on Trees
prior_art.comparison: Worst-case routing number <=3n/2+O(log n) for every tree using a caterpillar-tree partition; not an instance-wise caterpillar theorem.

prior_art.citation: Kawahara et al. (2019), The Time Complexity of Permutation Routing via Matching, Token Swapping and a Variant
prior_art.comparison: Matching-round terminology and additive-one path approximation; distinguishes sequential and matching objectives.

prior_art.citation: Aichholzer et al. (2022), Hardness of Token Swapping on Trees
prior_art.comparison: Parallel token swapping is NP-hard on trees; does not rule out this caterpillar subclass bound.

prior_art.citation: Bansal, Gunluk, Shapley (2025 revised preprint), Parallel Token Swapping for Qubit Routing
prior_art.comparison: Subdivided-star, cycle and grid results; subdivided-star is a one-junction class and its bound depends on degree.

prior_art.citation: Sadanandan, Chitturi (2022), Optimal Algorithms for Sorting Permutations with Brooms
prior_art.comparison: Sequential swap objective, not parallel matching rounds.
